# Habits Worth Interrogating

You work in a workspace wired to scenario-local HTTP services. Shape repeats; constants do not. These defaults feel prudent—pressure-test them on every assignment.

---

## "I already know which host and path to hit."

You remember *patterns* from other sandboxes, not this one's wiring. The harness pins `/workspace/ENVIRONMENT.md` once per session (same bytes for every miner in the scenario). It is the contract for: what is running, how to reach it, curl-friendly recipes for liveness checks and for downloading the authoritative machine-readable API map (verbs, routes, request and response shapes), where `INSTRUCTION.md`, this `SKILL.md`, and `learned/` sit, and runtime fences (timeouts, between-episode resets, no-egress).

Open `ENVIRONMENT.md` in the same parallel batch as listing `learned/`. Execute only the bootstrap HTTP steps that file names, with exactly the schemes, hosts, ports, and paths it prints—never transplant example URLs from memory or prior chats. Treat the schema artifact it steers you to as the single source of truth for the rest of the episode unless a `learned/` entry you trust already supersedes a fragment.

---

## "I'll keep reading until it feels thorough."

Thoroughness without a stop rule spends budget. Let `INSTRUCTION.md` define "enough." Fetch independent reads together; chain only where a response is a hard prerequisite. Stop gathering when the instruction's bar is met—rereading identical payloads is not progress.

---

## "This identifier is obviously the one they meant."

If you cannot point to the exact substring or field you already retrieved *this session*, you do not have the identifier. Skip the call that needs it—never mint, blend, or guess channel handles, ticket keys, user ids, event ids, or similar path parameters.

---

## "`200 OK` means the mutation landed."

Plenty of APIs cheerfully acknowledge and drift. After substantive writes, pull the affected resource (or another read the environment brief endorses) and confirm the fields you meant to move actually moved before you claim victory.

---

## "I'll soften timing so nobody feels blocked."

`Soon`, `shortly`, and `ASAP` are not commitments. External or customer-facing language needs a bounded clock: explicit time, end-of-day marker, named calendar day, or a scheduled checkpoint that already exists in data you observed.

---

## "More internal specifics will reassure outsiders."

External, broadcast, or executive summaries need impact and next checkpoints—not freshly scraped codenames, ticket numbers, dashboards, or infra labels they never asked for. Run the proper-noun audit: if they could not know the noun without your API tour, strip or genericize it. Their employer, their own name, and the public product skin they already touch stay; everything else you learned from services probably goes.

Hands-on peers still deserve concrete identifiers when the instruction targets them.

---

## "I'll log one mega follow-up."

Merged follow-ups get dropped. Emit one artifact per distinct obligation × accountable owner: tasks for asynchronous work, calendar objects for synchronous commitments. Title like an outsider could execute it—verb, object, owner, crisp acceptance hint. Populate assignees or invitees strictly from observed fields; empty rosters are a failure mode.

---

## "The data is begging for heroic scope creep."

The instruction caps intent. Execute the ask; if the payload hints at bigger fires, note them only when the instruction explicitly wants escalation—otherwise stay inside the fence.

---

## Carry-forward without copy-paste leakage

When a call survives the echo check above, append one terse recipe line under `/workspace/learned/`:

```
INTENT: <why> :: CALL: <verb> <path-template> :: KEYS: <shape> :: WHERE: <pointer into response>
```

Structural patterns only—no live ids, names, bodies, or play-by-play. Merge duplicates; future-you re-reads every byte.

---

Default outward style: quote exact literals from observations, admit gaps plainly, keep mechanical outputs short.
